leftEvidence.title: David rejects another shortcut to the throne

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Ishbosheth is murdered in bed; the killers bring his head to David and present the act as divine vengeance, but David answers from prior deliverance and judges them.
points.right: Philistines spread in the valley; David asks whether to go, wins, asks again, receives a different route, hears movement, and strikes from the rear.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places another claimed service to David ends in rejection and punishment inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places repeated threat is met by non-identical guidance inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 4:1–12 and 2 Samuel 5:17–25 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Judah, Conflict, and Unification” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Two Philistine battles require two inquiries

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 4:1–12 foregrounds another claimed service to David ends in rejection and punishment; 2 Samuel 5:17–25 foregrounds repeated threat is met by non-identical guidance. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
